articles.headline: Week 3 NFL highlights: Best plays, moments, touchdowns, more
articles.description: Sunday of Week 3 has seen 13 games played, with Lamar Jackson, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam Darnold having big stat days.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season continued Sunday with 14 games, including nine in the early window, and we'll have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In the early window, Jaylen Warren had a career outing in the Pittsburgh Steelers' win against AFC North rival Cincinnati Bengals, Jameis Winston stepped in to lead the New York Giants to a victory over the Tennessee Titans and the Washington Commanders slipped by the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Among the highlights from the afternoon slate of four games, the Baltimore Ravens stunned the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro on a Tyler Loop 56-yard field goal and the Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 after beating the Saints in New Orleans.

The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams in primetime to cap off the day, so keep checking here for "Sunday Night Football" highlights.

Week 3 highlights

articles.headline: Jackson's pass, alert timeout call lead to Loop's 56-yard field goal as Ravens beat Cowboys 34-31
articles.description: — Lamar Jackson completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers and alertly called a timeout with 1 second left, setting up Tyler Loop’s 56-yard field goal to cap a stunning 7-second drive that gave the Baltimore Ravens a 34-31 victory over the Dallas Cowboys...
articles.body:
RIO DE JANEIRO -- — Lamar Jackson completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers and alertly called a timeout with 1 second left, setting up Tyler Loop’s 56-yard field goal to cap a stunning 7-second drive that gave the Baltimore Ravens a 34-31 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in Brazil.


              The Ravens (2-1) and Cowboys (1-2) put on a entertaining show in front of an announced crowd of 72,792 during the NFL’s third game in Brazil and first in the city of Rio de Janeiro, engaging in a back-and-forth contest that featured plenty of big plays.


              For a moment, it looked as though it would be the Cowboys who would win the game in regulation.


              Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins was called for pass interference with 23 seconds left when his arms locked with CeeDee Lamb, giving the Cowboys the ball at the Ravens 2. After an incomplete pass, the Cowboys were called for a false start, which backed them up to the 7. Dallas settled for Brandon Aubrey's 23-yard field goal to tie it at 31 with 7 seconds left.


              And that set up the Ravens' improbable finish that was capped by Loop's kick sailing through the uprights and the jubilant Ravens swarming their kicker during a wild celebration at the Maracana.


              Jackson found rookie tight end Matt Hibner for a 2-yard touchdown for a 31-28 lead with 1:30 remaining. That gave the Cowboys and Dak Prescott enough time for the tying drive.


              Baltimore’s Derrick Henry ran for 89 yards and two touchdowns.


              The Ravens were in control with a 24-13 lead in the third quarter, but the Cowboys weren’t done. Jake Ferguson atoned for a previous turnover when Prescott found him for a 19-yard touchdown. Dallas added a 2-point conversion on a nice catch by CeeDee Lamb, cutting the deficit to 24-21.


              Baltimore appeared it was about to go up by 10 a few minutes later, but Henry was stuffed in the backfield on fourth-and-inches at the goal line when rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham sliced through the offensive line and made the tackle.


              Dallas kept the momentum in its favor with a 96-yard touchdown drive that included a 49-yard pass to Lamb. KaVontae Turpin had a 9-yard TD run to give the Cowboys a 28-24 lead with just under 10 minutes left.


              The Ravens’ defense came up big in the third quarter, forcing a Cowboys turnover when Ferguson fumbled a shovel pass from Prescott. Dallas tried for a 59-yard field goal later in the third, but Keondre Jackson blocked Aubrey’s kick to perserve the Ravens’ 17-13 lead and regain possession at mid field.


              Jackson hit Chris Moore for a 4-yard touchdown four plays later and a 24-13 lead.


              The Ravens recovered from a rough start, scoring 17 straight points to take a 17-13 lead into halftime.

articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第3週：日曜日の試合の要点、疑問点、ファンタジーの視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの取材記者がすべての試合に反応し、日曜日の各試合から浮き彫りになった最大の疑問に答えます。第3週から分かったことは以下の通りです。
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another  turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, while the Browns won their second straight game.

In the late window, the 49ers defeated the Cardinals despite a late comeback attempt. Quarterback Kyler Murray beat the Bucs in his first full game with the Vikings. And the Raiders stayed undefeated with a win over the Saints. 

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Raiders

With Kirk Cousins playing well, will Fernando Mendoza have to wait longer than expected? The Raiders know Mendoza's time to be the starter is looming, but he might have to wait a little longer. Cousins has the Raiders at 3-0 and has played well in the process. Against the Saints, Cousins completed 22 of 33 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns. He has thrown nine touchdowns in three games, and the team has fully embraced him as a leader. There's still no need to rush Mendoza on the field yet.

Key stat to know: Las Vegas scored 30-plus points in a game for the first time since its 63-21 win over the Chargers in Week 15 of 2023. They have scored at least 25 points in three straight contests. The Raiders only scored more than 25 points once during the 2025 campaign under former coach Pete Carroll. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Saints

What went wrong late for the Saints? Multiple turnovers were an issue in the second half. The Saints were playing backup left tackle Asim Richards with Kelvin Banks Jr. on injured reserve, and Richards gave up a sack that led to a fumble and points for Las Vegas. Later, Richards was backed up into Tyler Shough, who threw a wobbly interception as a result. The Raiders took the lead by scoring quickly afterward. The Saints had a chance to drive downfield and try to tie the game twice, but they turned the ball over -- again.

articles.headline: Judging the biggest overreactions to NFL Week 3 games
articles.description: Is Brock Purdy the MVP frontrunner? Are the Steelers going to have another winning season? We're judging Week 3 overreactions.
articles.body:
So we're through three weeks of the NFL season, and we don't know anything. And that's not an overreaction.

What in the name of John Madden happened on Sunday afternoon? The Seahawks gave up 33 points and lost to the Marcus Mariota-led Commanders? The Bills turned the ball over five times and still won? The stuck-in-the-mud Steelers rolled up 411 yards of offense to beat the red-hot, revamped Bengals defense? The Browns improved to 2-1?

Just when you think you can start to make sense of this season, you check the standings and wonder what's up with the 0-3 Chargers, 0-3 Texans, 1-2 Patriots, 2-1 Giants and the entire NFC West.

It's a reminder that it's still too early to draw any real conclusions about how this season is going to go and that so much of what we think we know is actually an overreaction. Which is the fun part, after all, right?

It's our Week 3 overreactions column, where we look at five potential takeaways and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational overreactions. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

Jump to:

Purdy is the next NFL MVP?

Giants are just fine with Jameis at QB?

The Steelers will avoid a losing season again?

Todd Monken will be Coach of the Year?

Mendoza isn't playing any time soon?

Fantasy overreactions

Brock Purdy should be the MVP favorite right now

Has any quarterback in the league been more efficient through the first three weeks? Purdy has completed 72.3% of his passes for an average of 263 passing yards per game. He's thrown nine touchdowns and one interception. He has rushed for 93 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries. The 49ers are bleeding wide receivers due to injury, and Purdy is just out there dicing up defenses like it's nothing.

His team is 3-0 with two division wins, including that opener in Australia against everybody's offseason darlings, the Rams. The last pick in the 2022 draft has turned into one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, and right now it's hard to find anyone playing the position any better.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

Oh, there are other candidates. Lamar Jackson just finished doing his thing in Rio. Patrick Mahomes will surely be in the conversation if the Chiefs keep it up. Josh Allen is also there, but he had a rough one Sunday despite Buffalo's win. Trevor Lawrence has been awesome in two out of three games. But no one makes a stronger case right now that Purdy, who just tied Steve Young's 49ers team record for most touchdown passes in the first three games of a season. The Niners haven't scored this many points in their first three games since 1998, which was the year Young did that. And he had Jerry Rice!

The Giants are going to be fine with Jameis Winston at quarterback

articles.headline: 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports
articles.description: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
articles.headlineJa: 「自分には関係ない」元マンC監督のマンチーニ氏、有罪報道を一蹴
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・マンチーニ氏は、自身が指揮を執っていた期間に犯したとされる財務違反について、古巣のマンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグから有罪と認定されたとする報道を一蹴しました。
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm. 

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
